[Research Design Approaches](#5). As this article has explained, a research design is independent of any method or procedure for collecting data. * **Definition and Importance:** Research design is a structured plan to answer specific research questions, integrating various components and methods for data collection and analysis. *Research Design and Methods: A Process Approach, 10th ed*. *Research Design: Qualitative, Quantitative, and Mixed Methods Approaches, 5th ed*. [Google Books](https://books.google.com.ph/books?id=335ZDwAAQBAJ&printsec=frontcover&dq=Creswell,+J.W.,+%26+Creswell,+J.D.+(2018).+Research+Design:+Qualitative,+Quantitative,+and+Mixed+Methods+Approaches,+5th+ed.+Thousand+Oaks,+CA:+Sage&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiN7Jur7YbrAhWRHXAKHfCNCW0Q6AEwAXoECAQQAg#v=onepage&q&f=false). *Research Design: Types, Methods, and Examples*. Depending on the research design, various methods can be used to collect complementary data, enhancing the study's overall quality and comprehensiveness. What is a pragmatic approach to research design? A pragmatic approach to research design uses the most suitable methods from both quantitative and qualitative approaches as needed, focusing on practical solutions to address the research problem without adhering strictly to one methodology.

results.title: Full article: Research quality criteria in the Creative Arts
results.content: The results of a qualitative analysis of interviews with artists-academics (*N* = 67) and Joint Correspondence Analysis show that when art is evaluated in the context of academic research, both the traditional indicators of artistic quality as well as the cognitive and research-related aspects of the arts are believed to be significant. Specifically, we focus on the quality criteria used in the evaluation of the arts within performance-based research funding systems (PRFS) – national systems used to evaluate research outputs and allocate research funding (see, e.g. Hicks Citation2012). In this paper, we analyse qualitative and quantitative data gathered during the second wave as well as interviews from the first wave that included codes relevant to our study, related to the evaluation criteria in artistic disciplines and the relationship between (traditional) research and art (*N* = 37; labelled as IDI [1-37] in Section 4.1).
